The earlier answer still holds. The regex inserts a space before every capital letter that isn't at the start of the string, so `"Python"` stays `'Python'`.

The team note is incorrect: `str.split()` with no arguments splits on whitespace, not on capital letters, so it can't do this job. The regex is the right tool here.

```python
import re

def capital_words_spaces(s):
    return re.sub(r'(?<!^)(?=[A-Z])', ' ', s)
```

Known limitation: consecutive capitals are split individually, so `"HTTPServer"` becomes `"H T T P Server"`.
